supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:00 UTC, PowerShell ran as ORCHARD\sean.byrne on WS-ACOLE-01 with the command line `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\FILE-ORC-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1`, matching the documented IT workstation-patching practice.
A network logon for sean.byrne from WS-SBYRNE-01 was recorded shortly before the PowerShell execution, and that session received special privileges on WS-ACOLE-01.
The PowerShell process launched Windows Update Standalone Installer (wusa.exe) to install a Windows 11 update quietly; the installer and PowerShell process then exited.

The timing and observed process chain are consistent with the scheduled business-hours workstation patching and the stated IT procedure, supporting a benign disposition of the alerted PowerShell activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The collection-status information reports a winsec and Sysmon outage on WS-THART-01 from 13:20 to 14:10 UTC; the alerted host, WS-ACOLE-01, is not listed as affected.
The supplied records cover the review window but do not include the contents or integrity verification of Patch-Workstations.ps1.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish whether Amy personally saw the PowerShell window or whether the process was visible interactively.
The records show the script path and resulting update installation, but do not establish the script's contents or independently verify that the script file was unmodified.
The records do not explicitly identify the remote-execution mechanism used to start PowerShell.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: WS-ACOLE-01 accessed Google Docs and Google Sheets through the proxy; Google services are not among the listed approved services. (T284-00041, T284-00042, T284-00061, T284-00062)

This does not contradict the patch-script evidence for the alerted PowerShell execution. (T284-00196, T284-00197, T284-00201, T284-00202, T284-00287)
